title: Field Report from Cuc Phuong National Park
transcript: Biodiversity conservation has become an urgent priority across Southeast Asia. In Viet Nam, national parks such as Cuc Phuong, Cat Tien, and Phong Nha-Ke Bang provide vital sanctuaries for rare fauna, including the Delacour's langur, the saola, and various endangered pangolin species. Habitat destruction caused by illegal logging, agricultural expansion, and poaching continues to threaten these fragile ecosystems. In response, wildlife rescue centres have initiated comprehensive rehabilitation programs where confiscated animals receive medical treatment before being reintroduced into protected wilderness zones. Local communities living near nature reserves are increasingly involved in community-based conservation, working as forest rangers and eco-guides rather than exploiting natural timber resources. Educational outreach campaigns in surrounding schools also teach students the value of native biodiversity and the devastating impact of the illegal wildlife trade. Protecting our natural heritage ensures that critical watershed forests and unique species will be preserved for future generations to cherish.
